title: Quote It Right
story: Unquoted variables split on spaces. A file called my notes.txt becomes two words and breaks things.
goal: Print each argument on its own line inside square brackets, like [one two]. Arguments may contain spaces.
hints: "$@" keeps each argument as one word.

for a in "$@"; do
  echo "[$a]"
done
socratic: What does $@ without quotes do to an argument with a space?
Where else do unquoted variables cause bugs?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Quote It Right”?
solution:
for a in "$@"; do
  echo "[$a]"
done
alt:
for a in "$@"
do
  printf '[%s]\n' "$a"
done
